name: Japanese

disabledReason.findWrongLetter: A substituted kana usually still reads as a plausible word fragment; the puzzle is not reliably solvable without a curated pair list.

notes: Every entry carries `word` (the normal written form, usually kanji) and `reading` (hiragana). tileField=reading tells the engine that all letter-level puzzles (unscramble, missing letter, complete the word, word ordering) operate on the HIRAGANA reading, one kana per tile — kanji are never split. Choice-style puzzles (multiple choice, meaning, category, emoji) show `word`. Small kana (ゃゅょっ) are their own tiles, which is how Japanese learners already see them in kana drills.
